identityReview: Mohammad Javad Zarif, January 8, 1960 Tehran; not Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani or a similarly named official. Resolve old CV narrative 1959 versus detailed 1960 in favour of current self-CV, detailed older CV and sanctions record. Denver MA/PhD international studies 1984/1988, SFSU international relations BA/MA 1981/1982. Former UN representative and foreign minister; strategic affairs vice president from August 1, 2024 with an August resignation/return episode, March 2025 resignation submission and formal acceptance April 15. Not first vice president or current foreign minister. PAIAB founder/president and Tehran associate professor stated in current institutional CV.
lifeStatusEvidence: ISSI records actual participation and attributed remarks at its September 23, 2026 Islamabad roundtable. PAIAB published a jointly signed article on November 8 with IRNA republication corroboration. Publication is evidence of recent public work, not an eyewitness proof of physical presence on publication day. October 2026 resurfaced video is explicitly described by The National as May 2025 remarks and is not used as a new October appearance.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read current PAIAB CV/essay, Denver university report, OpenTK parliamentary-CV mirror, contemporary confirmation reports, official EEAS agreement/implementation texts, Treasury designation, AFP resignation report, AP completed-acceptance account, Chatham House award paragraph and ISSI completed-event report. corrections: Read PAIAB current CV: January 8, 1960 birth; SFSU BA 1981/MA 1982, Denver MA 1984/PhD 1988; deputy foreign minister 1992–2002, UN permanent representative 2002–2007, foreign minister 2013–2021, strategic affairs vice president 2024–2025. Current institutional self-description is founder/president and Tehran associate professor of global studies. No claim of current government appointment from an institutional policy proposal.

Read University of Denver October 27, 2016 article. Awarding university identifies both 1984 MA and 1988 PhD as international studies. Older CV wording international law and politics is not silently substituted for the degree name. Joint Chatham House recognition and earlier offices corroborated; article’s loose received-this-week wording is not used to claim Zarif personally attended a London ceremony.

Read the OpenTK mirror of Dutch parliamentary document 2016D25347. Its narrative says 1959 but the detailed CV explicitly says January 8, 1960, Tehran; current PAIAB and Treasury data support 1960. Record this internal inconsistency rather than combine dates. Read document text via mirror, not independently authenticated original DOCX. Denver degree wording follows university account.

Read Asharq Al-Awsat August 17, 2013 report: parliamentary confidence votes held Thursday August 15, Zarif 232 in favour and 36 against. Confirmation date differs from publication date and earlier presidential nomination. Do not imply directly elected foreign minister or sole controller of Iranian foreign policy.

Read official EEAS July 14, 2015 Vienna statement PDF hosted by German Foreign Office: collective work, final JCPOA text agreed by Iran, EU and six countries, preceding Lausanne parameters April 2. Agreement text is not Implementation Day, bilateral work by only two people, or proof of lasting compliance. No exhaustive annex review claimed.

Read EEAS January 16, 2016 Implementation Day statement: contemporary IAEA verification and nuclear-related sanctions relief according to JCPOA. This historical statement does not establish all sanctions disappeared or uninterrupted compliance through 2026. Subsequent US withdrawal and implementation difficulties are separately sourced.

Read Treasury July 31, 2019 designation statement including operative opening and stated E.O.13876 basis. Date and rationale are attributed to the US administrative authority, not treated as an ICC conviction or independent judicial finding. This is historical designation evidence, not a full current sanctions-list or exemptions audit.

Read The New Arab August 25, 2021 substantive cabinet-confirmation report, separately from current navigation. Parliament approved Hossein Amirabdollahian as foreign minister as Raisi formed his government. Combined with PAIAB’s 2013–2021 term, this supports Zarif’s departure. Do not confuse presidential inauguration August 5 with successor ministerial confirmation August 25.

Read AFP/VOA March 3, 2025 report: resignation submitted and president had not yet responded; August 1, 2024 appointment, short August resignation episode and later return. March reporting alone does not establish formal presidential acceptance or first-vice-president status. Keep resignation submission distinct from later April acceptance.

Read AP by Jon Gambrell/Nasser Karimi in Durango Herald, dated Wednesday April 16, 2025. Text says presidency accepted resignation late Tuesday, hence April 15, and named Mohsen Ismaili successor. March submission and earlier 2024 rejected resignation are distinct. Read returned article text despite subscription controls appearing in the extraction; no login, subscription or access circumvention used. US 2018 withdrawal is historical context, not every later event independently audited.

Read relevant award paragraph in Chatham House July 25, 2017 AGM minutes: 2016 prize jointly to Kerry and Zarif for nuclear-deal negotiations; Zarif’s presentation took place later in Tehran. No claim all minutes reviewed or that this was a Nobel Prize. University and AGM wording about ceremony timing differ; public profile uses award year only.

Read ISSI September 23, 2026 completed roundtable report identifying Zarif as former foreign minister and quoting his intervention on shared security. It is an event report, not merely an invitation. No video/audio inspection or proof that his proposals were adopted by governments; used as actual recent participation evidence.

Read PAIAB November 8, 2026 essay by M. Javad Zarif and Ali Nasri. The authors advocate dialogue, ethical restraint and comparison of civilizational traditions. Attribution/date support recent publication; historical and geopolitical assertions throughout the essay are author positions, not independently verified facts adopted wholesale. Related-site November 12/13 articles are not assumed written by Zarif.

Read IRNA report and reproduced essay crediting Zarif and Ali Nasri and identifying PAIAB leadership. It corroborates the publication rather than independently proving every opinion in the essay. Returned body gives Sunday as original publication day but no explicit article timestamp; exact November 8 date taken from PAIAB, not invented as an IRNA timestamp.
